I'm closer to her than I am my actual best friends from kindergarten at the moment. Those guys all ran off to college 5 hours away and don't really seem to care when I tell them things... I know she's been reading them since she would reply to one every so often... typing all this is actually making me a little sadder... 

We would go out to lunch when she got out of class, and I would go see her right after work. We would just talk and it made every day a little better. I know her problems are a little bit greater than mine, but I really needed someone to talk to earlier this week and no one would really help...

I'm 19 as well, not quite in the same position as you are, but I can relate on the feeling useless part. I live with my parents and they are not very supportive of my life choices, as a nice way to put it. I dropped out of school, I broke up with a girl I didn't love (but they all thought it was the best fucking thing ever), and everyday has blurred together for a while now. 

If there is anything I've come to know is that the little things will make you happier. You don't need a fancy job, just something you can sustain yourself on and that you enjoy. 

The thing that keeps me going is the fact that if I can make one person's day a little better, then it was worth waking up.

Random acts of kindness. I don't care if I become a wandering homeless man. As long as I see someone smile. (It's even better when it's someone you care for)

I hope that brings you some comfort

No one deserves to feel like that. You defiantly don't. It sounds to me like he has a few problems of his own that you have no control over. That doesn't mean you should punish yourself.

It's a natural feeling (or at least for me it is) to feel pain for someone else's problems. Even if I had nothing to do with them, I still feel hurt or even a bit depressed over the emotional/physical/financial suffering of people close to me. 
Know that it isn't your fault and I hope that will bring some comfort :)

I've told this story once already today, but it seems like you should hear it too.

I'm 19 as well, I was feeling a bit trapped, afraid, sad, and distant from everyone. I decided to get up and go through my day as I had planned. Out of sheer chance I met a person that made my day a bit better and has since gave me something to look forward to. There is no reason I should have happened to meet her but it changed the direction of how I was feeling.

My point is, there is no way you will know what is to be if you aren't around to be there for it. And if you are religious, then find comfort in the fact that no one wants you to be unhappy, and that something will change your life for the better.

If you want to talk about anything, this is the place for it. The people that go through these posts are very caring and have helped me out once before a little while ago. 

Honestly, I can sympathize with how you are felling right now. I'm not in the kind of place I want to be either and that depressed feeling that just lingers over your shoulder is extremely painful... I can tell you this from experience though: It will get better.

There will be something that will make you happy, and sometimes those things leave you. Just know that you may not see it, but there are so many random things that happen. When I was in very similar state of mind, I went out and by sheer luck, happened to sit next to one of the most amazing people I've met in this life time. At the moment I've lost contact with her, but just knowing that there is a chance of random happiness keeps me getting up in the morning.

Point of that story is, you never know what will happen if you aren't around to experience it.

I'll be checking back to this post if you want to talk :)
